title: Vistect: Independent Visual Authorship
pitch: Vistect helps blind people understand and create visual documents with images, charts, and diagrams through structured, verifiable collaboration with their AI agent using WebMCP
about_excerpt: Vistect helps blind people understand and create visual documents with images, charts, and diagrams through structured, verifiable collaboration with their AI agent using WebMCP Like Comment Story Updates Vistect Independent Visual Document Understanding and Creation for Blind Professionals Inspiration Vistect began with a seven-hour wait. Arif Hosen is a Project Coordinator at Songjog Foundation, a nonprofit organization, and a member of our team. He is visually impaired and independently handles complex professional responsibilities, including coordinating projects, preparing communications, organizing information, and producing reports. During one project, Arif needed to create a press release and modify a project report card. He could write the content, organize the information, review the wording, and determine what the documents needed to communicate. The barrier appeared when he needed to add and modify visual elements, understand their placement, and verify the final layout. The document tools available to him did not provide sufficient nonvisual access to those visual operations. Arif had to wait for a sighted coworker to become available. He waited seven hours. The task itself did not require seven hours. The delay existed because the final visual layer of the work depended on access to someone else's sight. Arif was fully capable of producing the communication. The limitation was not his knowledge, judgment, creativity, or professional ability. The limitation was an interface that represented images, diagrams, charts, and layouts in a way he could not independently understand or control. That experience led us to ask: Why should a capable professional lose hours of productivity, privacy, and creative control simply because document software makes its visual layer inaccessible? That question became Vistect . What Is Vistect? Vistect is a WebMCP-native visual document workspace where blind and visually impaired people can understand existing visual documents and independently create, modify, inspect, and approve professional multipage documents. It combines two connected capabilities. Understand A user can open a visual document and explore: Pages and sections Headings and reading order Images and their purpose Charts and their underlying values Diagrams, nodes, connections, and paths Tables, icons, captions, and callouts Spatial relationships between visual elements Visual hierarchy and page composition Accessibility and layout problems Uncertain AI interpretations Create A user can create or modify a multipage document containing: Written content Uploaded images Contextual alternative text Icons Data charts AI-assisted diagrams Captions and source notes Structured page layouts Accessible reading order The user can then inspect the result using the same understanding system. This creates a continuous workflow: Understand → Create → Inspect → Validate → Correct → Approve → Export Vistect does not simply generate a document and ask the user to trust it. It gives the user structured access to what was created, how it was arranged, which decisions the agent made, which findings are uncertain, and what remains to be approved. The Independence Vistect Creates Before Vistect Arif could independently: Write a press release Organize its message Edit report content Review the text Determine what the document needed to communicate Make professional and editorial decisions However, he could still require sighted assistance to: Add or replace an image Understand where visual elements were positioned Select an appropriate photograph Modify a diagram Choose and inspect a chart Check spacing and alignment Detect overlapping or truncated content Verify that the exported document looked correct With Vistect A blind or visually impaired professional can: Understand the semantic and spatial structure of a multipage document Navigate by page, heading, image, chart, diagram, table, warning, or decision Inspect every important visual element Upload and compare image candidates Select images based on purpose, composition, tone, and relevance Crop and position images using semantic instructions Create and modify structured diagrams Trace paths and detect missing diagram connections Import data and create accessible charts Verify that a chart accurately represents its source values Detect measurable layout and accessibility problems Review changes made by an agent Approve or reject individual visual decisions Export the exact document version that was reviewed The transformation is not merely that document creation becomes faster. The transformation is that a professional task previously blocked until a sighted person became available can now be completed with much greater independence. Built With Lived Experience Arif is not merely the inspiration for Vistect. He is a member of the team whose workplace experience helped define the product. His experience changed our understanding of the problem. At first, it was easy to assume that the main challenge was generating visual elements. However, generation alone does not create independence. An AI can generate an image, chart, diagram, or document layout. But a blind user must still be able to answer: What exactly did the AI create? Why was this image selected? Does the image support my intended message? What is uncertain about its description? How are the objects arranged? Is every diagram node connected? Does the chart honestly communicate the data? Is any text overlapping or cut off? What did the agent change? Which visual decisions have I not approved? Does the exported version match what I reviewed? Vistect is designed around those questions. The goal is not to let AI make visual decisions for Arif. The goal is to provide enough structured understanding, operational control, validation, and transparency for Arif to make those decisions himself. “I was able to write the press release and work on the report card content myself. But when I needed to add and modify visual elements, I had to wait for a sighted coworker to help me. I do not need someone else to create the document for me. I need a tool that lets me understand and control its visual elements myself.” — Arif Hosen, Project Coordinator at Songjog Foundation and Vistect team member How Vistect Works Vistect represents a document as a structured semantic model rather than treating it as a flat visual canvas. The model contains: Pages Sections Text blocks Images Icons Charts Diagrams Tables Captions Spatial relationships Reading order Sources Accessibility descriptions Validation findings Visual decisions Approval states Document versions This allows Vistect to describe and modify the document through meaningful operations.
